question: What services does BPI offer?
html:
BPI is a communications firm working across political and advocacy campaigns, public affairs and corporate reputation, with paid media a large part of the mix (BPI public filings). A packaged monitoring-and-testing offering and named sector practices are planned but not yet in place (BPI growth plan).

What BPI does today

  • Political and advocacy campaigns. Federal committees paid BPI $115.3M in the 2024 cycle. Most of that was pass-through media spend, not BPI fee revenue (BPI public filings).
  • Public affairs and corporate advocacy. BPI serves corporate advocacy clients alongside political committees (BPI public filings).
  • Reputation work. The growth plan positions this for the AI era (BPI growth plan).
  • Paid media. The business is described as media-heavy, which weighs on margin (BPI public filings).

Where BPI works

  • BPI had 14 offices in 6 countries in Mar 2025 and has since added Boston (BPI public filings; BPI growth plan).
  • London is the #2 hub and Germany the #3 market (BPI growth plan).
  • Add-ons include BOLDT, UK firms closed Oct 29, 2024, Agado (May 2025) and 365 Sherpas (May 2026) (BPI public filings). The context does not say which service line each add-on brings.

What is being built

OfferingStatusScope
SignalOSPhase one, plannedNarrative monitoring, synthetic message testing and outcome dashboards, sold as always-on retainers
Named practicesPhase two, plannedAI and tech policy, energy and critical minerals, health (Boston), and litigation and oversight
Federal capture teamPhase two, plannedAbout $250M of tracked agency communications recompetes. BPI has no prime awards today

SignalOS will first be sold through the 2026 Reputation Resilience Index briefings. In that research, 81% of adults say AI makes false rumors too easy to spread (BPI growth plan).

What the data cannot show

  • Revenue by service line. No split exists in the context. A fee-revenue breakdown by service line from management accounts would answer this.
  • Current recurring share. The roadmap targets about 55% recurring revenue by Oct 2029 (est.), but today's share is unknown. A retainer-versus-project ledger would establish the baseline.

The service mix is the value gap. Political billings swung from $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024, so each dollar shifted into retainers and regulated-sector practices makes earnings steadier and supports the 10-13x exit range in the roadmap (est.).

Next actions

  1. Request a fee-revenue split by service line and client type for FY2024 and FY2025.
  2. Map each add-on's capabilities to the planned practices to find gaps for the next tuck-ins.
  3. Set a recurring-revenue baseline before SignalOS launches.
  4. Define the SignalOS retainer offer and pricing ahead of the Reputation Resilience Index briefings.
